A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original reward-poisoning experiments, policy-convergence measurements, and attackability-prediction accuracy on four RL environments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds synthetic linear-MDP sensitivity results in Appendix D.8–D.9 and Table 7.

M1.justification: The CQP characterization, white-box attack, and two-stage black-box procedure are retained, including their appendix implementations. Updated equation references and the NSE-to-NCE abbreviation correction do not change the algorithms.

E1.justification: Half-Cheetah, MountainCar, Pendulum, and FrozenLake remain. Appendix D.8 adds a focused synthetic linear-MDP evaluation under reward-parameter, transition, and feature-map noise.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain the same white-box, black-box, and AT baseline attacks against the same LSVI-UCB and CTRL victim settings. The AT citation changes from Xu and Singh (2023) to its 2025 publication without an identified comparator change.

E3.justification: The new sensitivity protocol uses (S,A,d,H)=(20,5,10,10), 100 instances per margin category, thresholds of ±0.1, and Gaussian noise levels 0, 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2. The existing benchmark budgets and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.8–D.9 adds the first dedicated study of CQP decision stability under parameter noise. Testing three noise sources across clearly attackable, near-boundary, and clearly robust instances substantially expands the robustness analysis beyond the existing benchmark attackability checks.

E5.justification: The existing 20-trial reporting and plotted uncertainty bands are retained. The new study reports percentages over generated instances without adding seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its noise levels are experimental conditions rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values and plotted trends are retained. New Table 7 reports near-boundary accuracy of 98%, 94%, 73%, and 60% as reward noise increases; clearly classified cases remain at 98–100%. New qualitative findings report no transition-noise sign flips and high sensitivity to feature noise.

T1.justification: Theorem B.5's proof corrects the union-bound stage range from h in [T] to h in [H]. The characterization, black-box cost theorem, formal assumptions, and remaining derivations are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract drops its explicit assertion that the framework efficiently attacks vulnerable instances, retaining the practical attackability-prediction claim. The necessary-and-sufficient characterization and white-box/black-box construction contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 explicitly warns that guarantees for learned linear representations need not hold for the original nonlinear environment. Appendix D.9 adds interpretations of noise sensitivity, including the direct effect of feature perturbations on CQP constraints.

D1.justification: Code-access instructions replace the anonymous repository with an identified GitHub repository. Conversely, the characterization-accuracy setup and Table 6 caption remove the explicit PPO attribution without identifying a replacement, reducing reproducibility detail without establishing an actual learner change.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained after matching titles across corrected author names and publication metadata. Changes such as Jin (2019) to Jin (2020) and Xu and Singh (2023) to their 2025 publication are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose and terminology corrections, expands the gap explanation, revises subsection hierarchy in Section 6 and Appendix D, and adds acknowledgments and a conflict disclosure. Author, publication, and bibliography metadata are also revised; the overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 7 is added, Table 6 moves beside its discussion, and existing figures shift position while retaining their plots. Figure 5's caption corrects 'attackable' to 'robust,' matching its existing panels and analysis. The first-page layout also changes.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity study and explicit warning about transferring representation-level guarantees improve assessment of practical reliability. These are limited gains alongside retained theory and benchmark results. Feature/transition-noise findings remain only qualitative, and removing PPO identification from Table 6 reduces reproducibility.
